definitions.explanation: An adnominal meaning 'unknown' or 'unfamiliar,' placed directly before a noun. Most often describes a person one has never met.

examples.japanese: {見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}に{道|みち}を{聞|き}かれた。
examples.english: A stranger asked me for directions.

examples.japanese: {見知|みし}らぬ{土地|とち}で{不安|ふあん}になった。
examples.english: I felt uneasy in an unfamiliar place.

examples.japanese: {夜道|よみち}で{見知|みし}らぬ{男|おとこ}に{声|こえ}をかけられて、{思|おも}わず{足|あし}が{止|と}まった。
examples.english: A strange man called out to me on the dark road, and I instinctively froze.

notes:
A {連体詞|れんたいし} (pre-noun adjectival): it appears only directly before a noun and does not conjugate. Literally 'not having seen and come to know.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}: a stranger; an unknown person
- {見知|みし}らぬ{土地|とち}: an unfamiliar place
- {見知|みし}らぬ{顔|かお}: an unfamiliar face

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {知|し}らない{人|ひと}: someone one doesn't know — more everyday and conversational
- {見知|みし}らぬ is slightly more literary, common in narration and writing
